options.feedback: Not yet. Calling it returns the captured `String` by value, giving it away; it can't do that twice.

options.label: `FnMut`
options.feedback: Not yet. `FnMut` closures can be called many times; this one gives away its only String on the first call.

options.label: `FnOnce`
options.feedback: Yes. The body moves `name` out of the closure, so it can only ever be called once.

hints: What happens to `name` when the closure is called? Could it be called a second time?
exercises.solution: The closure owns `name` (because of `move`) and its body returns it by value, moving it out. After one call there is nothing left to return, so the closure implements only **`FnOnce`**. Closures that only read their captures are `Fn`; those that modify them are `FnMut`.

options.label: `len()` needs the vector to be mutable.

hints: Which of `iter`, `iter_mut`, `into_iter` does a `for` loop over a plain vector call?
exercises.solution: A `for` loop calls `IntoIterator::into_iter` on its expression. For a `Vec<String>` by value, that consumes the vector and yields owned Strings, so `names` is moved and the final line uses a moved value. Loop over `&names` (shared references) to keep the vector.
